item.title: Reaction Start Lights
item.description:
How to Play

Wait for the five red lights to turn on one by one. After all five lights are lit, the game adds a random delay before the lights go out.

Press the mouse button or press Space as soon as the lights go out.

Scoring

  • A valid round measures the time between lights out and your mouse or key press.
  • Pressing before lights out is a false start.
  • The game tracks your best time, average time, and false starts across a short set of rounds.

Practice Tips

  1. Keep your eyes on the lights, not the result panel.
  2. Stay relaxed while waiting for the random delay.
  3. Use the same input method each time so your results are easier to compare.
  4. Try a few rounds, then rest. Reaction speed drops quickly when attention gets tired.

Most people improve after learning the rhythm, but the final random delay keeps the test from becoming a pure timing guess.

item.title: Cube Net Builder
item.description:
How to Play

Look at the colored cube. Choose the 2D net that could fold into that same cube.

The colors must land on the correct opposite and neighboring faces. Some options use the same colors but put one face in the wrong place.

Controls

  • Click a net to answer.
  • Drag the cube to rotate it and inspect hidden faces.
  • Press 1-4 to choose an option.
  • Press N or Space for the next question.
  • Press R to reset your score.

Practice Tips

  • First find opposite faces: top-bottom, front-back, left-right.
  • Then check which colors touch each other along an edge.
  • Rotate the cube view before answering if you need another angle.

This game supports geometry learning by connecting flat diagrams with folded 3D objects.

item.title: Mental Rotation 3D
item.description:
How to Play

Look at the 3D block shape on the left. Then choose which option shows the same shape after rotation.

The correct answer may be turned around in space, but the block structure is unchanged. Distractors may be mirrored, missing a block, or have one block moved.

Controls

  • Click an option to answer.
  • Press 1-4 to choose an option.
  • Press N or Space for the next question.
  • Press R to reset your score.

Practice Tips

  • Focus on corners, branches, and how many blocks touch each block.
  • Try mentally turning the whole object before comparing details.
  • Watch for mirror images. They often look almost right but cannot be rotated into the target.

This game is useful preparation for geometry, diagrams, engineering drawing, and other tasks that ask students to imagine objects turning in 3D.

item.title: Spatial Memory Training Game
item.description:
How to Play

Spatial Memory is a grid recall task. Watch the highlighted cells, then repeat the same sequence.

  1. Press Start.
  2. Watch the cells light up one by one.
  3. Click the cells back in the same order.
  4. Each correct round adds one more cell to the sequence.
  5. One wrong click ends the run.

Controls

  • Enter or Space: start or pause.
  • Esc or R: reset the current run.
  • Click or tap cells to repeat the pattern.

Difficulty Guide

Grid size Best for
3x3 First attempts and younger students
4x4 Standard practice
5x5 Advanced practice
6x6 Expert challenge

Start length controls how many cells appear in the first round. A start length of 3 is usually best.

item.title: Interactive Sudoku
item.description:
How to Play

Fill the 9x9 grid so that every row, column, and 3x3 box contains the numbers 1-9 exactly once.

The starting numbers are fixed. Your job is to reason out the empty cells.

Controls

  • Click a cell, then press a number button or use the keyboard keys 1-9.
  • Use Backspace, Delete, 0, or C to clear the selected cell.
  • Use the Arrow Keys to move around the grid.
  • Press H for a hint on the selected empty cell.
  • Press N to start a new puzzle.

A Good Solving Routine

  1. Scan rows and columns for places where only one number can fit.
  2. Check each 3x3 box and look for missing numbers.
  3. Use elimination: if a number already appears in the same row, column, or box, it cannot go in the selected cell.
  4. Slow down before guessing. Sudoku is most useful when each move has a reason.

Difficulty Guide

Level Best for
Easy Learning the rules and building confidence
Medium Regular practice
Hard Careful multi-step reasoning
Expert Longer challenge sessions

The game saves your current puzzle in the browser, so students can return later and continue.
